nodes.label: Mood Categories
nodes.rationale: 18 individual moods are collapsed into 6 coarse categories (Positive, Motivated, Anxious, Negative, Drained, Calm) so analytics stay legible: per-emoji trends would be too sparse to read, while six buckets still preserve emotional valence.

nodes.label: Mood Radar
nodes.rationale: A radar chart is chosen over a timeline because the interesting signal is the shape of the emotional distribution across categories, not a single series over time.

nodes.label: Animated WebP Mood Embed
nodes.rationale: Kept as the fallback embed because a plain tag works anywhere with no script, at the cost of a heavy file.

nodes.label: TGS Telegram Sticker Embed
nodes.rationale: TGS (gzip-compressed Lottie) is recommended over WebP: smaller files, faster loads, better mobile performance, smoother animation and lower bandwidth. The trade-off is that it needs tgs-player.js and a custom element instead of a bare .

nodes.label: Public/Private Mood Visibility
nodes.rationale: Embeds only work after /set_public, so mood data is private by default and the user opts in explicitly before anything is exposed on the web.

nodes.label: Personality Profile
nodes.rationale: Explicitly framed as an approximate self-report profile, not a clinical or medical diagnosis, to avoid implying diagnostic authority.

nodes.label: Personality Tests
nodes.rationale: Six tests (Mini-IPIP Big Five, communication, thinking/decision, conversation/emotional, behavioral, Big Five facets) are asked one question at a time with saved progress, so a long instrument can be abandoned and resumed inside a chat-style UI.

nodes.label: Gradual Profile Evolution
nodes.rationale: Weekly mood notes adjust the profile with small, validated, bounded updates. Big Five traits move slowly and communication preferences adapt faster, because personality is assumed stable while expressed style is not; bounding the step prevents one noisy week from rewriting the profile.

nodes.label: Compact Personality Context for AI Replies
nodes.rationale: A compact personality context steers tone and length of AI replies but is never revealed unless the user asks for their profile, keeping adaptation invisible rather than uncanny.
nodes.norm_label: compact personality context for ai replies

nodes.label: Talk AI Companion
nodes.rationale: Modeled on a warm, experienced psychologist (reflect, one gentle question at a time, small realistic ideas). Disclaimers are shown before every conversation because the product is an AI bot, not a therapist, and can be wrong. Conversations auto-end after 2 idle hours.

nodes.label: Risk Screening and Crisis Footer
nodes.rationale: Every message is quietly screened for self-harm, panic and hopelessness; on medium/high risk the reply pivots to immediate safety and appends a crisis footer, so safety handling does not depend on the user asking for help.

nodes.label: User-Supplied OpenAI Key
nodes.rationale: AI features run on each user's own OpenAI key (/set_openai_key), verified once and stored encrypted and masked. This moves inference cost and data responsibility to the user, at the price of AI features being off until a key is set.

nodes.label: Settings Tab
nodes.rationale: Model choice defaults to gpt-5.6 but accepts any typed model id, so users are not blocked waiting for the catalog to be updated.

nodes.label: Admin Tab
nodes.rationale: Admins are granted by hand in MongoDB (is_admin flag) rather than through any in-app flow, and can view any user's personality radar regardless of that user's sharing setting.

nodes.label: Public Personality Link (/p/<token>)
nodes.rationale: A token URL shows a standalone personality card to anyone, and sharing is off by default so the link only exists once the user opts in.

nodes.label: Personality Catalog Seeding
nodes.rationale: Traits, tests and questions live in MongoDB collections seeded at start-up from src/personality/catalog.seed.js with a version bump, so new instruments can be added as data rather than code changes.

nodes.label: Cron Scheduling
nodes.rationale: Cron jobs drive daily reminders and weekly analytics/insight passes rather than on-demand computation.

nodes.label: Node Test Runner with In-Memory MongoDB
nodes.rationale: Tests use Node's built-in runner plus an in-memory MongoDB so no external service is needed; MONGODB_TEST_URI overrides it when a real server is wanted.
nodes.norm_label: node test runner with in-memory mongodb

nodes.label: bot service (docker-compose)
nodes.rationale: A single container built from the repo root runs both the Telegram bot and its HTTP server; restart: unless-stopped keeps the long-lived bot polling across host restarts.

nodes.label: Bot Environment Configuration
nodes.rationale: Every setting (tokens, Mongo URI, channel ids, cron times, base URL, key-encryption secret) is injected from the host environment rather than baked into the image, with SERVER_BASE_URL defaulting to https://moodpal.samanfekri.me.

nodes.label: External shared-network
nodes.rationale: The compose file joins an externally managed network instead of creating one, so MongoDB and a reverse proxy live outside this stack and are reached by service name.

nodes.label: Host 8080 Port Mapping
nodes.rationale: Host port is pinned to 8080 while the container port follows SERVER_PORT, so a fronting proxy can target a fixed port regardless of the app's internal choice.

nodes.label: MoodPal Mini App (Vue root)
nodes.rationale: One single-file Vue app serves two modes chosen from location.pathname: the authenticated Telegram mini app, and a public read-only personality card at /p/<token>.

nodes.label: Self-Hosted Vendor Libraries
nodes.rationale: Vue and tgs-player are served by the app itself (/public/lib/...), never from a public CDN, per an explicit comment in the head - removing a third-party runtime dependency and the privacy leak of CDN requests.

nodes.label: Telegram Theme Token Fallbacks
nodes.rationale: Every CSS custom property reads a --tg-theme-* variable with a hardcoded light/dark fallback, so the same page looks native inside Telegram and still renders correctly when opened in a plain browser.

nodes.label: Splash Failure Fallback
nodes.rationale: A 12s timer turns the loading splash into a reload prompt, and a synchronous typeof Vue check fails fast if the bundle never loaded - the mini app webview gives no other error surface.

nodes.label: waitForTgsPlayer
nodes.rationale: tgs-player registers window.TgsPlayer asynchronously after it fetches lottie/pako, so the app polls every 50ms with a 10s timeout instead of assuming the global exists.

nodes.label: MOOD_HUES / CATEGORY_HUES
nodes.rationale: A hue per mood code and per personality category drives card glows, so color encodes meaning consistently across every surface without per-component styling.

nodes.label: radar (computed)
nodes.rationale: Shows Big Five when measured, otherwise the category with the most traits, capped at 8 axes and requiring at least 3 traits - a radar with too few or too many axes is unreadable.

nodes.label: api (fetch helper)
nodes.rationale: All authenticated calls go through one helper that sends X-Telegram-Init-Data, forces cache: 'no-store', dedupes in-flight GETs by path, and retries GETs up to 3 times with backoff only on network or 5xx errors - writes are never retried.

nodes.label: isStale
nodes.rationale: A 30s STALE_MS window with a per-tab fetchedAt timestamp means tab switches re-render instantly from memory and only refetch when data has aged - cheap caching without a store.

nodes.label: watchActivation
nodes.rationale: Telegram keeps the mini app alive in the background, so visibilitychange, window focus and the Telegram 'activated' event all trigger a staleness-gated refresh; a 5s grace period after open prevents a double fetch on launch.

nodes.label: ensureLoaded
nodes.rationale: Safety net: a tab that renders with no data and no recorded fetch requests its own data, covering paths where setTab was bypassed.

nodes.label: fetchMe
nodes.rationale: Re-POSTs /auth rather than calling a dedicated endpoint, because /auth already returns myMood, isAdmin and the share link in one round trip.

nodes.label: updateMood
nodes.rationale: The mini app does not render a mood picker: it asks the bot to post the picker into the chat and then closes itself, reusing the bot's existing keyboard flow as the single source of truth.

nodes.label: mountStickers
nodes.rationale: TGS players are instantiated lazily through an IntersectionObserver with a 200px rootMargin, falling back to loading every element when IntersectionObserver is missing; a failed player load degrades to a static failed state rather than an empty card.

nodes.label: destroyStickers
nodes.rationale: Lottie players are explicitly destroyed on refresh, tab change and beforeUnmount, since each one holds a running animation loop that would otherwise leak in a long-lived webview.

nodes.label: setupMainButton
nodes.rationale: The Telegram MainButton is bound to 'Add a friend' only on the Friends tab, and hidden elsewhere and during a quiz, so the native button never contradicts the visible screen.

nodes.label: shareUrl
nodes.rationale: Three-tier degradation: Telegram's openTelegramLink share sheet, then the Web Share API, then clipboard copy with a toast.

nodes.label: openFriend
nodes.rationale: A friend's personality request that fails is treated as { shared: false } rather than an error, so a private profile and a failed fetch present identically and leak nothing.

nodes.label: answer
nodes.rationale: The server returns the next question (or the finished profile) with each answer, so the client never holds the whole instrument; a 410 means the session expired and the quiz is closed and re-synced instead of retried.

nodes.label: closeQuiz
nodes.rationale: Closing an unfinished quiz keeps the latest session so 'Continue' resumes at the exact question, distinguishing dismissal from cancellation.

nodes.label: fetchAdmin
nodes.rationale: Paginates with append-or-replace semantics, lazily loads the trait catalog once, and translates 403/401 into distinct operator-facing messages (not an admin vs. reopen from Telegram).

nodes.label: TRAIT_LEVELS filter buckets
nodes.rationale: Continuous 0-1 trait values are exposed to admins as any/low(0-0.4)/mid(0.4-0.6)/high(0.6-1) ranges, turning a numeric filter into three meaningful buckets.

nodes.label: searchAdmin
nodes.rationale: Debounced at 300ms so keystrokes do not each hit the paginated admin query.

nodes.label: openAdminUser
nodes.rationale: Personality loads in parallel (fire-and-forget) while the mood history awaits, and both guard on the sheet still showing the same user so a fast re-tap cannot cross-populate another user's data.

nodes.label: loadMoreMoods
nodes.rationale: Cursor pagination on next_before rather than offsets, so appending older moods is stable while new entries arrive.

nodes.label: toggleAdminFriend
nodes.rationale: After a friend add/remove it refetches the Friends tab and resets sticker state, keeping the two tabs consistent instead of relying on staleness to catch up.

nodes.label: saveKey
nodes.rationale: The key is cleared from the input after POST and the server's masked settings object is what re-renders; 400 means malformed key, 401 means OpenAI itself rejected it - two different messages.

nodes.label: loadPublic
nodes.rationale: Public mode parses the token straight from location.pathname, calls /api/public/personality/<token> without any auth header, and sets document.title from the response - one page serves both the authenticated app and an unauthenticated share card.

nodes.label: formatWhen
nodes.rationale: Timestamps are rendered relative to calendar-day boundaries (Today/Yesterday/weekday/date) rather than elapsed milliseconds, and drop the year when it matches the current one.

nodes.label: freshness
nodes.rationale: Moods are graded fresh (today) / recent (<=3 days) / stale, giving each friend card a color cue for how current the mood really is.

nodes.label: Flat Minimal Icon Style (White Disc on Blue Field)
nodes.norm_label: flat minimal icon style (white disc on blue field)
